title: Finite element approximation of a variable-exponent flow
paper: Pulsatile Flows for Simplified Smart Fluids with Variable Exponent Power-Law: Analysis and Numerics
figure: Figure 9, left panel; non-even case in Section 7.2 (equation 7.5 per repository README)
transformation: Vector PDF extracted with crop [0, 0, 478, 381.467] pt. Plot curves, numeric axes, colors, labels and legend are unchanged. No new solver run and no estimated/digitized numerical data.
meaning: Red step lines: p(x)=2.5 for x≤0.5 and p(x)=1.5 for x>0.5 on (-1,1). Solid blue: exact stationary benchmark v. Dashed blue: nine finite element approximations evaluated at final time L. Purple: prescribed flux alpha. The example illustrates a steady nonlinear benchmark inside the pulsatile-flow study; it is not a measured flow or a time sequence.
caption: Finite element velocity profiles approach the exact asymmetric benchmark for a discontinuous material exponent. Dashed curves show nine refinement levels; the red steps indicate p(x), and the purple line is the prescribed flux.
alt: Exact velocity profile and nine finite element approximations for a non-even variable-exponent flow. The approximations approach an asymmetric profile as the discretization is refined; the material exponent decreases from 2.5 to 1.5 at x=0.5.
